sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how Java treats primitive types like objects! Wrapper classes are your new best friends when you need to work with primitives in an object-oriented way.

• What wrapper classes are and why they exist
• How to convert between primitives and objects automatically
• Practical uses of wrapper classes in real code

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a party where everyone speaks different languages. Primitives (like `int`, `double`) speak 'basic data', while objects speak 'fancy Java'. Wrapper classes are like translators that help them communicate!

Java provides wrapper classes for all primitive types:
• `Integer` for `int`
• `Double` for `double`
• `Boolean` for `boolean`
• And more for all other primitives

These classes 'wrap' the primitive value in an object, giving you superpowers like:
• Storing numbers in ArrayLists (which only hold objects)
• Using methods to convert between types
• Handling null values safely

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Each primitive type has a corresponding wrapper class: int/Integer, double/Double, char/Character
Autoboxing automatically converts a primitive to its wrapper: Integer x = 5
Unboxing automatically converts a wrapper to its primitive: int a = x
Wrapper classes provide utility methods like parseInt(), toString(), and MAX_VALUE
Wrappers are needed where objects are required (e.g., collections like ArrayList)

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Wrapper classes bridge the gap between primitives and objects. Autoboxing and unboxing make conversions automatic and painless. Always handle null values when working with wrapper objects. Practice using wrapper methods like `parseInt()` and `valueOf()`.

questions.question: Why are wrapper classes needed in Java?
options: To allow primitive values to be used where objects are required
questions.explanation: Wrapper classes (Integer, Double, Character, etc.) allow primitive values to be treated as objects. This is needed for collections like ArrayList that can only store objects.

questions.question: What is autoboxing in Java?
options: Automatic conversion of a primitive to its wrapper type
Converting a wrapper to a primitive
Packaging classes into a JAR file
questions.explanation: Autoboxing is Java's automatic conversion of a primitive type to its corresponding wrapper class. For example, Integer x = 5; automatically converts the int 5 to an Integer object.
